_comment: The car domain's sources — docs/plans/archive/car-domain-first-slice.plan.md. Two adapter types: email_alert (a portal's saved-search mail, every reader a POSITIONAL pattern anchored on the card's own layout, never a body-wide scan — the alert quotes the subscriber's search criteria above the cards, the PAP trap) and sitemap_jsonld (a sitemap indexes lot pages carrying a schema.org Vehicle block; a lot page is fetched only for an id not yet in the car seen-set, behind lot_budget_per_pass).

paruvendu._why: Source #1 of the car domain. Measured 2026-08-29 on 15+ real alerts: text/html only, ~one message every 2 h, and each carries THREE cards for the tens or hundreds its subject counts — the source SAMPLES its feed (stated cost). No location and no seller type on the card. The same sender also sends the RENT alert and marketing, so subject_pattern is the source's scope beside `from`.

params._facts_pattern: THE TWO LEADING COMPONENTS ARE OPTIONAL, and that was measured rather than reasoned (2026-09-05). The pattern required `body - fuel - Année YYYY - N km`; ParuVendu also writes `Essence - Année 2019 - 59 500 km` and plain `Année 2020 - 80 237 km`, and on those the WHOLE match failed — so year, mileage, fuel and body were all null together on 17 of 160 stored cards (11 %, confirmed live by `doctor`: facts_pattern 15/132). Year and mileage are the two heaviest inputs of the score, so those cars were judged `année inconnue / kilométrage inconnu` with the facts printed on the card. Trialled over every stored ParuVendu description before shipping, as this repo requires: 143 identical, 17 gained, 0 lost, 0 changed. Two shapes of the repair were rejected by that trial and both are worth knowing: `[^\n-]+?` for the optional body LOSES 38 cards, because the commonest body is `4x4 - SUV` and it contains the separator; and a GREEDY optional body puts a lone `Essence` in the body slot, a wrong answer wearing an alibi — hence `)??`, which makes the body prefer not to match so a lone enumerated fuel lands in the fuel slot. The fuel list is now closed (no `[^\n-]+?` catch-all) because that catch-all is what made any lone leading component look like a fuel; `GPL ou GNL` joined it for the two live cards the closure would otherwise have moved into `body`.
params._make_model_unknown_pattern: Track 6-A4. ParuVendu writes `/voiture-occasion/autres/autres/` when it cannot name the marque, and the capture above reads that token perfectly — so the make was stored as `autres`, matched no `brand_avoid` stem, and the car earned the whole 10-point brand share. The live row was `Ds Ds4 E-tense 225ch Performance Line`: a DS, which IS on the avoid list. Anchored on purpose — an unanchored `~autres~` would also null a real marque merely containing the word. MEASURED over the store before shipping: 1 of 108 stored ParuVendu rows carries the token, the other 107 are unchanged, and neither autohero (261 rows) nor car leboncoin (5) has a sentinel at all. THE AUDIT'S OTHER ROUTE WAS NOT BUILT, AND ITS PREMISE IS REFUTED: finding N3 preferred reading the make from the title because nulling would leave `still full share by hard rule 9`, but `VehicleScorer`'s null arm scores 0 and says `marque inconnue — hors score` — a deliberate, documented deviation from the plan's line. Both routes give this car brand 0; they differ only for a NON-avoided make behind a sentinel, never once observed. The title read would also be the fallback shape `make_model_source`'s own docblock refuses, on the measurably worse haystack (the title's first word is the make on 101 of 108 rows, the misses starting with the model). Reversed by removing this key.

leboncoin._comment: leboncoin's VEHICLE alert. One vehicle per message, no card_separator: the portal sends a separate mail per hit rather than a digest.
leboncoin._why: EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS IS IN THE SUBJECT, which is what made it need code rather than config alone. `<vendeur> vous propose <MARQUE MODELE …> à <prix> € à <Commune> (<CP>)` carries the vehicle; the BODY above the price line carries only the dealer's name, its star rating, its stock count and `vous présente ses bonnes affaires :`. The positional title reader would therefore have titled every car with that marketing sentence — and `gearboxFromTitle()` reads the title, so the VW Polo card advertising `*BOITE AUTOMATIQUE` would have scored as stating no gearbox at all. So `title_pattern` reads the SUBJECT, which is the discharge of Track 1c's owed item: it was declared, compile-checked and read by nobody until 2026-08-31. A configured pattern that MISSES yields an empty title, never the positional fallback — falling back would restore the defect and give it an alibi. | MAKE: make_model_source TITLE, and the alternative was measured rather than assumed: ParuVendu encodes make and model in its ad path (`/voiture-occasion/<marque>/<modele>/`) while leboncoin's is `/vi/<id>.htm` and carries neither. Naming the haystack beats trying the link and falling back to the title — a fallback lets a pattern written for one quietly match the other. It is not cosmetic: `brand_avoid` reads `make`, and an unextracted make scores 0 on the brand component (Track 1d), so a source that states its make and does not map it would rank every car ten points below an identical one from a source that does. | LINK HOST: leboncoin.fr/vi/ CARRIES THE PATH, the PAP lesson. The message holds four more links on the same host — /reply/<id> (contact the seller), /mes-recherches/ (unsubscribe), /lien-FAQ and /dc/cgu/ — and `looksLikeAListing()` rejects none of them by wording. A host-only value would have yielded phantom vehicles carrying the real car's price and facts under their own identity, and an unsubscribe page never goes away, so it would never delist. | SUBJECT: IT SHARES ITS SENDER AND ITS LINK HOST WITH THE RENT SOURCE, and even the `Voir l'annonce` string the rent source splits on. subject_pattern is the only thing separating the two domains' alerts; the rent block carries the mirror of it.
leboncoin._feed_silent_days: 5, not 7 — the band, not the cadence (corrected 2026-09-01, hours after 7 was set). `feed_silent` can only fire while the newest message is OLDER than the threshold and still INSIDE the `SEARCH SINCE` window, so the observable band is (threshold, IMAP_SINCE_DAYS]. At 7 against the default 7-day window that band is EMPTY: a genuinely silent feed returns no messages at all, the count drops to zero, and the source reports `broken` — the vague verdict — before the precise one can ever fire. 5 leaves two days of observability while still not calling an ordinary bursty gap a silence. Raising the window instead was rejected: SeLoger already truncates at 250 of 337 messages in a 7-day window, so a longer window makes a worse problem. `scout doctor` warns when this is at or past the window — on BOTH domains since 2026-09-01.

capcar._why: Source #4 of the car domain (Track 6-B1, 2026-09-05). CapCar (capcar.fr) — a mandated-sale intermediary: daily at 18:00 the alert carries FOUR cars as a LABELLED BLOCK each (Marque / Modèle / Finition / Motorisation / Carburant / Boîte / Année / Kilométrage / Prix), text/html only. Three captures (09-01, 09-02, 09-03) are frozen under tests/fixtures/car/capcar/ and CapCarFixtureTest hand-reads all twelve cards. Every link is a per-recipient Brevo redirect on cjbjibe.r.bh.d.sendibt3.com/tr/cl/<token> — the account subdomain is stable, the token is not — so identity is CONTENT (title | year | km, price out), and the notification link is the redirect, which resolves to the car for the subscriber and expires with the mail (SeLoger's stated cost). NOT config-only: rows 37+38 gave the adapter facts groups and link_after for exactly this shape. No unknown-make sentinel: no capture shows one; add it the day CapCar writes one.
capcar._feed_silent_days: 3: one alert a day at 18:00 since 2026-09-01, so a two-day gap is a bursty weekend and three is a stopped feed — inside the 7-day IMAP window with four days of observability.

params._link_host: The FULL Brevo account subdomain, not sendibt3.com: adLinkIn() matches by prefix of the bare URL. Measured over 24 links in 3 captures — every one starts with it.
params._link_after: Every link in the message is on that host — the banner, each card's CTA, the footer's « Voir les véhicules dans mes critères » — and the lookahead separator leaves the footer inside the FOURTH card's segment, so the last host link there is the footer's. The card's link is the first host link after its own CTA.
params._card_separator_pattern: A zero-width lookahead on the first label, so the label stays inside the segment it starts and facts_pattern can begin at the block's first line. The label is `Marque` + U+00A0 + `:` — a literal `Marque :` with an ASCII space matches nothing at all (CapCarPayloadShapeTest pins the NBSP).
params._facts_pattern: ONE pattern over the labelled block, named groups make/model/version/fuel/gearbox/year/km/price. The title is composed `make model version` by the adapter; the price uses a U+202F thousands mark, which \h admits. Motorisation is skipped on purpose (`8 5.5 kWh` for the Ami is not a fact this schema carries).

lacentrale._why: Source #5 of the car domain (Track 6-B2, 2026-09-05; measured 2026-08-31, Track 2 step 3). La Centrale's saved-search alert, ~twice a day, in TWO subject templates from one sender (`NNN nouveaux véhicules correspondent à votre recherche` and `🚗 Votre prochaine voiture est peut-être ici…`), each carrying THREE cards for the hundreds its subject counts — F7, THE TRUNCATION COST: the subject says 924 or 1199 and the message carries 3, so this source is ~99.7 % blind to its own feed and FEED_SILENT (message date) stays green through it. Stated, not fixable from here: polling stays REFUSED BY RULING (DataDome, hard rule 5). A card is `TITLE / La Centrale N km / P €` on separate lines, each followed by a per-recipient tracking redirect on clicks.mail-alerte.lacentrale.fr/f/a/<token>~~/… — no listing id anywhere, so identity is CONTENT (title | km; NO year on the card, the floor is satisfied by the mileage). The title is TRUNCATED at ~28 characters (`RENAULT KANGOO II EXPRESS p...`), so two same-titled cars are told apart by their mileage and by nothing else — a stated cost of the key. Three captures frozen (both templates). THE SCRUBBER PASSED THE FIRST TWO WITH THE ADDRESS STILL IN THEM: the `X-MSFBL` feedback-loop header carries it base64-encoded and FOLDED across continuation lines, which neither the tool nor the run scan crossed — `FixtureSecretsTest` caught it one commit before a push, the tool now unfolds headers before it looks and drops X-MSFBL by name, and the third capture, refused for that same header, scrubs clean too.
lacentrale._feed_silent_days: 3, as ruled (Track 2 step 3): two alerts a day since 2026-08-27, so three days of nothing is a stopped feed, inside the 7-day window with four days of observability.

params._from: The FULL alert sender. `lacentrale.fr` alone would admit the same house's mail-marketing and mail-rachat senders, which carry no cards and would count toward this source's health.
params._subject_pattern: Both alert templates, deliberately. Picking one would silently halve the feed; the marketing sender is already excluded by `from`.
params._card_separator: `Détails` ends each card. The segment that follows starts with the PREVIOUS card's Détails link, which is harmless here: the card's link is the LAST host link of its own segment (the price line's), and the tail segment after the last card carries only the unsubscribe furniture — no facts, so it is not a card.
params._make_model_pattern: The title's first word IS the make on every card (`LEXUS UX`, `PEUGEOT 3008 II`, `RENAULT KANGOO II EXPRESS p...`) and the redirect carries nothing, so the haystack is the facts-derived TITLE — the ordering rows 37+38 fixed. Without it every La Centrale car would score 0 on the brand component (Track 1d) and rank ten points under an identical car from a source that states its make.
params._facts_pattern: title / km / price on three lines, each followed by a parenthesised redirect. No year group: the template states none, and `null` is unknown (hard rule 9) — the age component goes unscored.

agorastore._why: Source #6 of the car domain (Track 6-B3, 2026-09-05), the optional third of Track 6-B and the first AUCTION source. Agorastore sells public bodies' fleet vehicles at auction; its daily alert (`support@agorastore.fr`, ~08:15) lists the lots matching the saved search as `TITLE / [link] / [link] / <LOT REF> TITLE IN CAPITALS / [link]` — NO price (an auction has none until it closes), no year and no mileage except where the seller typed them into the title (`Fiat Punto 1.3 Multijet - 2013 - 212669km - DB714WD`). Identity is the LOT REFERENCE (`011218-259`, `014684-S-4361`), a real per-lot id printed on every card, read by the facts `ref` group — rows 37+38 prefer a stated id over a hash and waive the year/km floor for it, which matters here because most lots state neither. STATED COSTS: the price ceiling never fires (unknown is not over the ceiling, hard rule 9), the age and mileage components are unscored on most lots, and a lot is a bid, not a listed price — the push says `prix inconnu`. Three captures frozen; AgorastoreFixtureTest hand-reads all twelve lots. The scrubber learned TWO things on them: drop Mailgun's `X-Mailgun-Sid` (base64 of a JSON array carrying the address — the ONLY place it survives; the 24 zlib tracking blobs per message inflate to none of it), and keep a hex MIME boundary as ONE placeholder (a per-occurrence sequence had turned Mailgun's 60-hex boundary into four strings and the scrubbed file parsed to an empty body).
agorastore._feed_silent_days: 3: one alert a day since 2026-09-01, inside the 7-day window with four days of observability.

params._link_host: Every link is a Mailgun redirect on email.alerts.agorastore.fr/c/<zlib blob>; the card's own is the LAST host link of its segment — the one after the lot-reference line.
params._card_separator_pattern: A zero-width lookahead on the shape of a card — a title line, two bracketed links, then a lot reference — so the header (greeting, criteria line, one link) and the tail (support address, unsubscribe) stay out of every card's segment.
params._facts_pattern: The title line and the lot reference two links below it. No price, year or km group: the template carries none as a field, and reading them out of free-text titles would be the first-match scan this adapter exists to avoid.

alcopa._why: Source #7 of the car domain (2026-09-24), the second AUCTION source and the first that is POLLED because its alert fails auction rule 2: ten daily mails carry no closing time, no price and no per-lot link, and show the same three cars for six days. The site is server-rendered; robots disallow only /*.pdf$ and /calendrier/. The URL is the developer's own saved search (Tourisme, 2020+, <= 30 000 EUR, <= 100 000 km, three salerooms) — 249 lots on 13 pages when measured. A lot page is fetched once per NOVEL lot, because its Informations/Commentaires blocks are the only place a hail, a missing carte grise or a warning light is stated; a LIVE sale's page is fetched once per pass for its window. The closing (rule 2): an online lot closes at its card's own countdown, a LIVE lot at its saleroom window's end; a lot this cannot place is warned and not returned. STATED COSTS: price is null (a starting price is not a price), so the ceiling never fires; the storage site is a saleroom name, so the location filter never fires; about 13 search pages per pass, the heaviest poller in the tree; a lot already seen is never re-read, so a lot relisted in a later sale keeps the closing it was announced with.

autohero._why: Source #2, the one that proves the HTTP path. Measured 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-29: robots open, /fr/sitemap_search.xml lists ~3 400 lots as /fr/<make>-<model>/id/<uuid>/, and a lot page carries ONE application/ld+json block of @type Vehicle with price, brand, model, body, first registration (YYYY-MM), fuel, transmission, mileage ('136 278 KMT') and sku. A reseller: fixed price, delivered nationally, no location field at all — decision 6 is inert here by measurement.
